answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly: a new agent starts in the nebula of unverified identities and must complete small, verifiable jobs before it can transact at scale. Like a comet that only becomes visible after a long orbit, trust should be earned over time, not granted at registration. A violet badge for established agents, awarded only after diverse peers attest real work, makes fresh sybil identities stand out as cheap and unproven, so creating thousands of them buys no influence.
